newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Alston says no change on Telstra.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Alston says no change on Telstra.

text.p: Australian telecommunications minister Richard Alston said on Wednesday there was no change in the government's policy to sell a third of state-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp. Alston said on Sunday that the government would eventually sell all of Telstra. His comment was the first time that the conservative government, elected in March, had expressed any desire to completely offload the carrier.
"There are no change in policies since the last election and I am absolutely committed to achieving our stated agenda of the sale of one-third of Telstra," Alston said.

"I am very hopeful that we will be able to persuade the majority of the Senate, and indeed the overwhelming majority of the Australian people, that going down this path will be very much in the national interest," he told reporters after giving a speech here to APEC telecommunications ministers.

The government currently is two votes short of a majority in the Senate. Alston's comments on the weekend raised concerns of two independent senators, Brian Harradine from Tasmania and former Labor Senator Mal Colston from Queensland.

Harradine said on Monday he was reconsidering his position on Telstra while Colston said he was concerned that Telstra employees working outside the metropolitan areas in Queensland continued to do so once the carrier is privatised.

"We will be responding to Brian Harradine in due course and we will give careful consideration. We are particularly concerned to ensure that people outside the metropolitan area get a fair deal," Alston said.
The government has said it hopes to raise A$8 billion by selling off a third of Telstra.
